# The German level test — a review by our teachers

*Generated from the live question bank. Please do not edit this file by hand —
tell us what to change and we will update the test itself.*

---

## What this is

A short online test that tells a person which level they should join: A1, A2, B1, B2 or C1.
It sits on our website to bring in new students, and we will also use it on a tablet at the
front desk when someone walks in.

**It is not an exam.** It does not replace what you do in the classroom, and it does not decide
anything on its own — we always confirm the level with the student before they start. Its job is
to get people close enough to the right course that the conversation starts well.

It tests **reading, grammar and vocabulary only.** There is no speaking, writing or listening in it.
The result page says so plainly.

## What we need from you

Four questions, for each of the 50 items below. It should take about 45 minutes.

1. **Is it at the right level?** Would a student at this level get it right, and a student one level
   below get it wrong?
2. **Is there exactly one right answer?** *This is the one that matters most.* If a native speaker
   could defend one of the other options, the question is broken and has to go.
3. **Is the German natural?** Something a person would actually say or write.
4. **Is anything important missing?** If a level tests something we always teach and it is not here,
   tell us.

## How to tell us

Every question has a code — `B1-06`, `A2-03`. Write the code and what is wrong with it. That is enough.
Print this and mark it up, or send the list by email. You do not need to suggest a replacement,
though we will take one gladly.

---

## How the test decides someone's level

**The test is in sets of 6 questions.** One set per level.

It starts by asking the person how much German they already know, and begins at roughly that level.
Then it moves:

| Out of 6 questions | What the test does |
|---|---|
| 5 or 6 right | They know this level — go **up** a set |
| 3 or 4 right | They are in the middle of this level — **stop here** |
| 0, 1 or 2 right | Too hard — go **down** a set |

Most people answer 2 or 3 sets, so 12 to 18 questions in total.

**The level we report is the level they should join** — the first level they have *not* mastered.
Someone who gets all the A2 questions right and half the B1 questions right is told **B1**,
because B1 is what they still need to learn.

### An example

Someone says they can hold a conversation, so the test starts at B1.

- **B1 set:** 6 out of 6. They know B1 — go up.
- **B2 set:** 3 out of 6. They are part-way through B2 — stop.
- **Result: B2.** They join a B2 course.

Had they scored 1 out of 6 on that first B1 set, the test would have gone *down* to A2 instead.
It corrects itself in both directions, so it does not matter much if someone misjudges themselves
at the start — it only changes how many questions they answer.

### One thing this means for your review

There are **10 questions per level in this document, but each person only sees 6 of them**, picked
at random. We do that so two people sitting next to each other do not get the same test.

So the ten questions at a level need to be **about equally hard**. If one of them is much harder
than the rest, some students get an unfairly difficult set purely by luck. If you spot an odd one
out, that is exactly the kind of thing we need to hear.

### `B1-10`  ·  reading  ·  gist

> Liebe Nachbarinnen und Nachbarn,
>
> am Samstag renovieren wir das Treppenhaus. Von 9 bis 16 Uhr ist der Aufzug außer Betrieb. Wer Möbel transportieren möchte, sollte das bitte vorher oder an einem anderen Tag tun.
>
> Vielen Dank für Ihr Verständnis!

**Was sollen die Nachbarn am Samstag beachten?**

- ✅ Der Aufzug kann tagsüber nicht benutzt werden.
- Das Treppenhaus ist den ganzen Tag gesperrt.
- Möbeltransporte sind am Samstag günstiger.
- Der Aufzug wird am Samstag repariert.

### `B2-10`  ·  reading  ·  inference

> Dass Homeoffice die Produktivität steigert, gilt inzwischen als gut belegt. Weniger eindeutig ist jedoch, wie sich die dauerhafte Abwesenheit vom Büro auf den Zusammenhalt in Teams auswirkt. Erste Langzeitstudien deuten darauf hin, dass der informelle Austausch – und damit womöglich auch die Innovationskraft – darunter leidet.

**Was lässt sich dem Text entnehmen?**

- ✅ Die Wirkung auf den Teamzusammenhalt ist noch nicht abschließend geklärt.
- Homeoffice senkt nachweislich die Produktivität.
- Langzeitstudien belegen, dass die Innovationskraft zunimmt.
- Der informelle Austausch im Büro gilt inzwischen als überschätzt.

### `C1-10`  ·  reading  ·  stance

> Die Debatte um die Reform wird mit einer Vehemenz geführt, die in keinem Verhältnis zu ihrer tatsächlichen Tragweite steht. Wer sich die Mühe macht, die Gesetzestexte zu lesen, findet vor allem Präzisierungen des Bestehenden. Von dem Paradigmenwechsel, den beide Lager beschwören, kann keine Rede sein.

**Welche Haltung vertritt die Autorin?**

- ✅ Die Aufregung um die Reform steht in keinem Verhältnis zu ihrem Inhalt.
- Die Reform bedeutet einen grundlegenden Wandel des Systems.
- Beide Lager unterschätzen die Folgen der Reform erheblich.
- Die Gesetzestexte sind für Laien kaum verständlich formuliert.

## Thank you

Once we have your notes we will fix the questions and send this back for a second look.
Any question the two of you disagree about, we will drop rather than argue over — a question
teachers cannot agree on is not one we should be asking students.
